title: Binary/text framing, FIX-style and ITCH-style records

objectives.text: Derive FIX-style length/checksum and binary record boundaries from versioned byte contracts without treating text splits or raw structs as protocol parsers.
Validate narrow schema/range/unit/identity constraints before state mutation, separating framing/checksum success from session completeness, authentication and market/account truth.
Validate the complete synthetic bar-delimited grammar before its SOH-valued checksum, preserving textual tags and explicit scope limits.

blocks.markdown: Keep transport framing, message encoding/schema, session sequencing and application state separate. TCP is a byte stream; UDP is a datagram transport without delivery/order guarantees. FIX tag-value encoding and Nasdaq ITCH are message formats carried with their session/transport layers. Nasdaq TotalView-ITCH is outbound market data, NOT an order-entry instruction interface. A decoded Add Order describes a displayed feed event under its specification; it is not our confirmed order, a personal fill or permission to send a trade.

FIX tag-value fields use numeric tag=value and the actual one-octet SOH delimiter (0x01), not a printable vertical bar. Common session framing begins with BeginString(8), then BodyLength(9), MsgType(35) as the third field and CheckSum(10) last. BodyLength counts octets AFTER the delimiter ending 9 through the delimiter immediately before 10. CheckSum is the three-digit decimal representation of the sum modulo 256 of octets from the start through the delimiter before 10, excluding the 10 field. Literal bars in logs may be display substitutions, not wire bytes. Unicode character count and a split on text characters are not substitutes for exact octet accounting.

blocks.title: Count the body, not an attractive substring

steps.text: Own tiny framing fixture body is bytes 35=0<SOH>, length 5. Its head is 8=FIX.4.4<SOH>9=5<SOH> followed by those 5 body octets.
Compute modulo 256 over that complete head, format exactly three decimal digits and append 10=ddd<SOH>. The 7-octet trailer is outside BodyLength and outside its own checksum sum.

The tiny body omits required session fields on purpose: a framing test can pass while full FIX schema/session validation fails. A checksum is not authentication, encryption or an application acceptance acknowledgement.

blocks.caption: Expected output: True, then length or trailer mismatch. The bounded complete-frame checker returns raw body, not a parsed/session-validated message. It accepts only FIX.4.4 prefix and own 1..200-octet body policy, checks three-digit modulo checksum and final delimiter. A real TCP reader must first accumulate partial header/body/trailer and keep subsequent frames separately. No socket/session/logon/order or full FIX compatibility is implemented.

blocks.markdown: Read the versioned ITCH5 Add Order A format: type at 0; stock locate at 1 length 2; tracking at 3 length 2; timestamp at 5 length 6; order reference at 11 length 8; side at 19 length 1; shares at 20 length 4; stock at 24 length 8; price at 32 length 4. Total 36 octets. Integer fields are big-endian and unsigned unless stated; alpha is ASCII left-justified and space-padded on the right. Price(4) is integer units of 1/10000, not cents or a native floating double. The retrieved specification caps Price(4) at 200000.0000. Timestamp is nanoseconds since midnight, not an epoch timestamp or a UTC date by itself.

blocks.source:
def decode_add_a(record):
    # Narrow ITCH5 Add Order A subset, not full exchange feed/book validation.
    if type(record) is not bytes or len(record)!=36 or record[:1]!=b"A":
        raise ValueError("expected 36-octet Add A")
    locate=int.from_bytes(record[1:3],"big")
    timestamp_ns=int.from_bytes(record[5:11],"big")
    reference=int.from_bytes(record[11:19],"big")
    side=record[19:20]
    shares=int.from_bytes(record[20:24],"big")
    stock_bytes=record[24:32]
    stock=stock_bytes.rstrip(b" ")
    price_units=int.from_bytes(record[32:36],"big")
    if not locate or side not in (b"B",b"S") or not reference or not shares:
        raise ValueError("invalid own order subset")
    if timestamp_ns>=86400*10**9 or not 1<=price_units<=200000*10000:
        raise ValueError("invalid own time or price subset")
    if not stock or any(not 65<=x<=90 for x in stock) or stock_bytes!=stock.ljust(8,b" "):
        raise ValueError("expected own uppercase symbol subset")
    return locate,timestamp_ns,reference,side.decode("ascii"),shares,stock.decode("ascii"),price_units

record=(b"A"+(1).to_bytes(2,"big")+(0).to_bytes(2,"big")+(123).to_bytes(6,"big")+
        (7).to_bytes(8,"big")+b"B"+(100).to_bytes(4,"big")+b"ABC     "+(1234500).to_bytes(4,"big"))
print(len(record))
print(decode_add_a(record))
blocks.caption: Expected lines: 36; (1, 123, 7, 'B', 100, 'ABC', 1234500). Price units 1234500 represent 123.4500, not 12345 dollars or 1234500 cents. The code imposes own stricter subset: nonzero locate/reference/shares/price, timestamp inside a non-leap 86400-second day, uppercase A-Z symbol with canonical padding. It is not the complete exchange symbol/calendar/domain policy. It preserves locate/timestamp/reference/side/shares/symbol/price but not tracking metadata; full provenance must retain raw record/session/venue/version separately.

blocks.markdown: Check bytes/type/total length before offsets; check declared message type/version before interpreting that layout; then validate field codes/ranges/units and required business mappings. Reject unsupported message types rather than pretending every record is Add A. A fixed 36-byte length is not enough: side X, malformed symbol, invalid declared bound or wrong session remains invalid for our interface. Stock locate must be mapped consistently to the stock directory under the correct feed/session. A reference is day-scoped by the source contract, not globally unique forever. No arbitrary native struct layout/padding/endian reinterpretation is a safe portable wire decoder.

Real FIX includes required headers, session IDs/sequence state, heartbeat/logon/reset/resend and application dictionaries/repeating groups/data fields with their own length semantics. Do not generalize a raw SOH split or flat dict that overwrites duplicate tags into a general FIX parser; repeating tags can be valid inside schema-defined groups. This lesson validates only the explicit complete framing fixture and narrow Add A subset. The checksum can detect some byte errors but collisions are easy: increasing one byte and decreasing another preserves the sum. Neither checksums nor asserted SenderCompID authenticate a peer.

Independent transfer: recompute FIX BodyLength/checksum with an independent byte counter; alter one byte without updating checksum and reject it, then show a deliberately adjusted colliding sum is not an authentication proof. For Add A, encode known multibyte values independently, test every truncation, wrong side/type, boundary price and symbol padding. Keep integer price precision until explicit display conversion and retain raw/session/version metadata. Do not send these fixtures to any exchange or broker.

Sources read: [FIX encoding standard description](https://fixtrading.org/packages/fix-tagvalue-encoding/), [FIX Session Layer June 2020](https://www.fixtrading.org/wp-content/uploads/download-manager-files/FIX_Session_Layer_June_2020.pdf), [Nasdaq TotalView-ITCH5 specification](https://www.nasdaqtrader.com/content/technicalsupport/specifications/dataproducts/NQTVITCHSpecification_5.0.pdf), and [MoldUDP64 transport](https://www.nasdaqtrader.com/content/technicalSupport/specifications/dataproducts/moldudp64.pdf). Protocol-specific facts follow the retrieved documents, while toy bounds/acceptance restrictions are explicitly own policy. Passing examples is not protocol certification or live market connectivity. The FIX encoding package page identifies the standard; exact BodyLength/checksum byte boundaries are additionally corroborated by the [vendor FIX header description](https://docs.deribit.com/fix-api/production/overview), not by the package summary alone.

A log grammar, not a full FIX session parser

This practice input replaces every SOH byte with a printable vertical bar and guarantees printable ASCII without spaces. Every field, including the checksum field, ends in a bar. Its own grammar requires one equals sign, a nonempty value, a one-to-four ASCII-digit tag and no duplicate TEXT tag. Thus 55 and 055 are distinct, not integer aliases. The first tag is exactly 8 and last exactly 10. Tag 10 value must be exactly three ASCII digits. Do not import real FIX BodyLength/header/session/group requirements absent from this exercise, and do not relax real FIX validation to this flat grammar.

Structural errors precede checksum errors

First require a trailing bar, remove exactly that one delimiter, and split fields. Preserve empty pieces: a doubled final bar creates an empty field and is BAD_FORMAT. Scan every field and reject duplicate tags before computing the checksum, even if a prefix already has a mismatch. A checksum that happens to match cannot rescue malformed grammar. The values dictionary is populated only after each field passes the no-duplicate check; overwriting duplicates would lose the evidence.

Checksum bytes and extraction

Checksum covers the prefix through the delimiter immediately before 10=, not the checksum field or its ending bar. Sum ASCII codes for ordinary characters but 1 for each bar, then reduce modulo 256 and format three decimal digits. Once verified, return OK followed by tags 35,55,38,44 in that order, or - for each absent tag. Missing tag 35 is allowed here despite the real session layout discussion. Checksum is weak error detection, not authentication or proof of an accepted order.

Trace, work and transfer

For prefix 8=F|, the checksum is 56+61+70+1=188, so 8=F|10=188| is well formed and returns OK - - - -. Replacing 188 by 189 yields BAD_CHECKSUM; adding a duplicate 8 field yields BAD_FORMAT regardless of checksum. With up to 10000 lines of length 400, total work is linear in input characters and per-message state is bounded by that line. Test all grammar failures, tag 55 versus 055, absent extraction fields and checksum-prefix boundaries with an independent byte-oriented SOH reconstruction. This is private synthetic parsing, not sending messages to a venue. The current corrected visible FIX.4.2 example has prefix byte sum 2010 and checksum 218. Its former checksum 065 counted printable bars incorrectly and is now an explicit BAD_CHECKSUM regression; do not reproduce the old example as valid.

from collections import OrderedDict, deque
from bisect import bisect_left
import heapq
import math

def parse_messages(messages):
    lines = []
    for message in messages:
        if not message.endswith('|'):
            lines.append('BAD_FORMAT')
            continue
        fields = message[:-1].split('|')
        tags = []
        values = {}
        valid = True
        for field in fields:
            if field.count('=') != 1:
                valid = False
                break
            (tag, value) = field.split('=')
            if not 1 <= len(tag) <= 4 or not tag.isascii() or (not tag.isdigit()) or (not value) or (tag in values):
                valid = False
                break
            tags.append(tag)
            values[tag] = value
        if not valid or not tags or tags[0] != '8' or (tags[-1] != '10') or (len(values['10']) != 3) or (not values['10'].isascii()) or (not values['10'].isdigit()):
            lines.append('BAD_FORMAT')
            continue
        prefix = '|'.join(fields[:-1]) + '|'
        checksum = sum((1 if char == '|' else ord(char) for char in prefix)) % 256
        if f'{checksum:03d}' != values['10']:
            lines.append('BAD_CHECKSUM')
        else:
            lines.append('OK ' + ' '.join((values.get(tag, '-') for tag in ['35', '55', '38', '44'])))
    return lines

print(*parse_messages(['8=F|10=188|', '8=F|10=189|', '8=F||10=000|']), sep='\n')

summary: Parse a versioned octet contract before applying state. FIX body length/checksum and ITCH binary offsets/price precision are different layers from session identity, valid market state and authenticated application acceptance. Narrow fixture success is not full protocol compatibility. Practice transfer: bar log checksum parser.
